transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-30
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Ava (Redwood SE), Ravi (Redwood CSM), Marta (Garland VP Eng), Devon (NetOps), Priya (Platform), Eli (Security), Jonah (SRE)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
- Kernel upgrade last week correlates with 20-30ms p95 jump for short responses.
- Canary rollback in staging showed reduced jitter for 512 token requests.
- Egress shaping and MTU mismatch still plausible; packet captures requested.
- Action: rollback test, telemetry dashboard link, security deep-dive.

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir Patel: hey everyone, thanks for jumping on, we'll call this the week five pilot netops sync for Garland Bio. ava and I will run through what we saw in the last 48 hours and then we'll go into triage.
[00:12] Marta Ruiz: thanks Samir, quick note - got Execs breathing down about the p99 blips during our demo last friday so we want to understand root cause.
[00:19] Ava Chen: yep, understood. quick show of hands, who saw the 11:30 spike? jonah?
[00:24] Jonah Park: yeah I was on pager, saw a bunch of small errors, latency bump kinda like stair steps.
[00:30] Devon Blake: for context we pushed kernel 5.19.7 to the nodes in the private pool last thurs, that aligns with the timeline.
[00:38] Ava Chen: exactly, so we ran a controlled canary on friday night - in staging we rolled back to 5.18.x and the p95 dropped by ~22ms on average for small payloads. not perfect but consistent.
[00:50] Eli Navarro: just to flag security, during the kernel swap we also rotated some module signing keys - nothing suspicious but want to keep KMS logs in the loop.
[00:58] Samir Patel: good call. can you, eli, confirm whether KMS rotations happened before or after the rollout?
[01:02] Eli Navarro: it was after, we did a scheduled rotation on friday at 23:45 UTC, which is after the initial deploy. logs show no access anomalies.
[01:10] Ava Chen: thanks. two candidate buckets: kernel-level scheduler/irq handling change, and network-level egress shaping / MTU mismatch. we also saw KV cash warmup weirdness - sorry, KV cache - where prefix caching wasn't effective for the short session burst.
[01:28] Devon Blake: on egress shaping, our edge devices have an explicit policy that shifts packets when burst > 20MB in 1s per connection, could be interacting with the model streaming pattern.
[01:40] Priya Singh: also noticed occasional fragmentation on large responses, MTU on the tunnel is 1400 on the contraption vs 1500 expected, so fragmentation + reassembly could add micro delay.
[01:52] Samir Patel: that's super helpful. ava, did the telemetry point to any particular hop?
[01:56] Ava Chen: per the traceroute and APM, we see small RTT increases hitting the egress gateway and then relatively flat to the model pool. the increase seems concentrated during token-heavy short sessions.
[02:08] Jonah Park: i dumped a pcap during the spike window and I can see ICMP fragmentation and lots of TCP retransmits which could explain jitter.
[02:16] Devon Blake: sending that pcap now to the shared folder.
[02:19] Samir Patel: perfect. two immediate experiments agreed: 1) staged kernel rollback test (Ava), 2) egress shaping bypass for a canary subset (Devon), 3) MTU normalization test on one tunnel (Jonah).
[02:33] Marta Ruiz: timeline wise we need initial results within 48 hours because we have a customer demo next tuesday.
[02:39] Ava Chen: that's tight but doable. we'll prioritize the rollback since it had the clearest perf delta.
[02:44] Ravi Malhotra: side note on observability - we noticed some sparse telemetry retention; we're going to flip on higher-res traces for the pilot nodes for the next 72 hours. that will increase cost but gives us detail.
[02:55] Priya Singh: fine with that for the short window. can you also share the Grafana link and the retention changes?
[03:00] Ravi Malhotra: yes, I'll share the dashboard link.

[03:10] (15m into call)
[03:10] Ava Chen: quick demo of the Grafana panel - p95 token latency, egress gateway latency, and kernel context-switch counters. you can see before rollback vs after in staging.
[03:22] Marta Ruiz: can we annotate which deploy caused the change? that'll help with postmortem.
[03:27] Ava Chen: already annotated last friday's deploy and the kernel bump. there is a noticeable uptick in context-switches after 5.19.7.
[03:35] Devon Blake: context-switches up could be IRQ balancing differences, i recall that kernel introduced some new NIC driver behavior.
[03:41] Samir Patel: driver changes could explain both IRQ and packet pacing differences, which looks like both our candidate buckets.
[03:47] Eli Navarro: security check - is the influx of retries exposing any PII via logs? we need to ensure our log redact rules applied across the pipeline.
[03:55] Priya Singh: logs are redacted at the agent level, but the raw pcaps have IPs; we'll avoid sharing those in public channels.
[04:02] Ava Chen: noted. we'll use sanitized pcaps.

[04:20] (mid-call triage)
[04:20] Ava Chen: experiment plan detail: staging rollback to 5.18.9, run load generator for 2 hours at small prompt sizes, collect p50/p95/p99 and traceroutes. then, on private pool, carve out one canary route to bypass egress shaping - that should isolate network impact.
[04:38] Devon Blake: bypassing shaping is doable for 10% of traffic, we can route to a direct egress path. but we need a circuit breaker in case of egress spikes.
[04:46] Samir Patel: Redwood can add a per-route token-based circuit breaker to protect the backplane; we'll enable a 10rps soft-limit for the canary.
[04:54] Jonah Park: also recommend enabling continuous KV cache pre-warm for the canary, to avoid cold-start tail latency.
[04:59] Ava Chen: yes that's part of it - prefix caching config change to keep top-20 prefixes warm for the canary. we'll document the config.

[05:20] (customer questions)
[05:20] Marta Ruiz: on the fallback policy - can Redwood automatically fallback to a quantized model during spikes?
[05:27] Samir Patel: yes we support model variant routing; we can create a policy to route to a lower-cost quant variant when p95 exceeds threshold or when egress latency crosses X ms. but two notes: output quality and hallucination profile will differ, we should evaluate with your prompt sets.
[05:41] Priya Singh: good, schedule a quick eval with our prompts. we have some domain-specific safety checks.
[05:47] Samir Patel: we'll include an eval harness and sample prompts.

[06:00] (security thread)
[06:00] Eli Navarro: what about SSO and SAML onboarding for the console access during the pilot? we need to ensure RBAC maps correctly to roles and that audit logs are shipped to our SIEM.
[06:09] Ava Chen: we support SAML and OIDC, and we can forward audit logs to your Splunk instance via secure syslog. we have a short onboarding guide - I'll share it.
[06:18] Eli Navarro: KMS - Redwood's Private deploy uses customer-managed KMS or HSM?
[06:23] Samir Patel: in Private we support integrating your KMS (AWS KMS / GCP CMEK) or HSM via our connector. for the pilot you opted for Redwood-managed keys with audit-forwarding; for production we'll switch to team-managed keys.
[06:36] Eli Navarro: okay that tracks, just want it in the ticket.

[06:50] (telemetry deep dive)
[06:50] Ava Chen: one oddity - the KV cache metric shows warmups that look like spikes exactly at hour boundaries; likely a cron job on your side clearing sessions. can you confirm any scheduled jobs?
[06:59] Priya Singh: yes, we run a cleanup at 00:00 UTC and at 12:00 UTC, it's a retention TTL flush. that could explain periodic cold starts.
[07:07] Ava Chen: if that's expected we can adjust prefix cache TTLs to survive that flush for the canary.

[07:20] (logs & artifacts)
[07:20] Devon Blake: uploaded two pcaps to the shared drive (pcap-20250530-1132, pcap-20250530-1145) and the MTU dump. folder link: https://redwood.share/garland/pilot/pcaps (note: placeholder link).
[07:35] Samir Patel: thanks Devon. I also uploaded the fallback playbook and a sample canary checklist: https://redwood.share/garland/pilot/playbook.

[07:45] (planning next steps)
[07:45] Ava Chen: timeline recap: rollback test in staging by EOD tomorrow, canary egress bypass for 10% traffic in 48 hours, MTU normalization test in parallel, security deep-dive scheduled for next week.
[07:57] Marta Ruiz: sounds good; one ask - can you include a short risk summary for the rollback (what could go wrong)?
[08:03] Samir Patel: yes, short doc with rollback risks (driver mismatches, potential driver regressions, need to reboot some nodes) - I'll send that by EOD.

[08:15] (closing)
[08:15] Ravi Malhotra: i'll push higher-res traces and share dashboard link in the thread.
[08:20] Samir Patel: excellent. quick recap on action items (verbal): Ava - rollback test + report; Devon - pcaps and egress bypass; Jonah - MTU normalization test; Samir - pricing + rollback risk doc; Eli - confirm KMS rotation timestamp in ticket.
[08:34] Marta Ruiz: appreciate the focus. we'll aim to have the demo on tuesday but will confirm after the results.
[08:40] Ava Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up in the thread with links.
[08:45] (call ends)

Notes on transcription quality: speaker overlaps occasionally labeled as single speaker, some product names transcribed roughly (e.g., KV cash), timestamps are approximate.
